entries.name: Ask PRAXIS
entries.methodology: Ask PRAXIS answers from the attached User Core and Situation Core, then routes the next step to writing, research, graph repair, or a specialist policy tool. It should explain the basis for the answer, show gaps, and propose actions before writing into the workspace.
entries.limits: It is a command plane, not an automatic mutation engine. Tool runs and graph updates remain confirmation-gated.

entries.name: Context Builder
entries.methodology: Context Builder is the intake and repair gate. It checks whether the situation has enough scope, actors, sources, mission framing, assumptions, and graph structure before heavier AI work runs.
entries.limits: It strengthens the case file but does not replace expert source judgment or full graph review.

entries.name: Grounded Research
entries.methodology: Grounded Research proposes defensible sources ranked by recency, diversity, and reliability. It checks the situation corpus first to avoid duplicates, then returns a search plan, source receipts, and gaps still missing from the Source Graph.
entries.limits: Fresh web coverage depends on provider availability and the specificity of the situation frame.

entries.name: Stakeholder Map
entries.methodology: Stakeholder Map visualizes alliances, adversarial dyads, third-party postures, power, legitimacy, urgency, leverage, and Track I/II/III positions so the analyst can see who matters and why.
entries.limits: Actor salience is only as strong as the Situation Core and source coverage.

entries.name: Position vs Interest
entries.methodology: Position vs Interest separates stated positions from underlying needs, constraints, red lines, BATNAs, and possible issue bundles. It helps PRAXIS move from actor description to negotiation strategy.
entries.limits: It should be rerun when actor incentives or mandates change.

entries.name: Scenario Projector
entries.methodology: Scenario Projector identifies uncertain high-impact drivers, projects best/likely/worst trajectories, and names indicators that would move probability. It keeps time horizon and warning signals explicit.
entries.limits: Scenario probabilities are structured judgments, not forecasts with statistical certainty.

entries.name: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses
entries.methodology: ACH compares hypotheses against evidence, forcing disconfirming evidence and weak assumptions into view. It is the default PRAXIS method when a core judgment may be overfit to a single narrative.
entries.limits: The matrix is only useful when hypotheses are meaningfully distinct and evidence is attached.

entries.name: Contradiction Finder
entries.methodology: Contradiction Finder reviews a claim, memo, or tool output for unstated assumptions, source diversity issues, motivated reasoning, missing intelligence, and evidence that would change the conclusion.
entries.limits: It critiques reasoning quality; it does not independently verify every cited source.

entries.name: Frame Narrative
entries.methodology: Frame Narrative explains how actors describe the situation, which frames are gaining traction, where legitimacy claims diverge, and how a memo or briefing should avoid adopting an unexamined frame.
entries.limits: Narrative reads need fresh media/source coverage and should be caveated by language and platform gaps.

entries.name: Coalition Detector
entries.methodology: Coalition Detector looks for clusters, brokers, dependencies, patrons, and likely alignment shifts. It turns the Situation Core into testable graph proposals rather than just prose about relationships.
entries.limits: Coalition inferences should be reviewed before mutating the canonical graph.

entries.name: Commitment Tracker
entries.methodology: Commitment Tracker records obligations, deadlines, verification mechanisms, compliance posture, and violation type. It is the PRAXIS memory for promises that need follow-up.
entries.limits: It needs temporal anchors and source receipts; vague political statements should be marked as weak commitments.

entries.name: Memo Drafter
entries.methodology: Memo Drafter turns the active User Core, Situation Core, sources, and selected tool outputs into a reviewable work product in PraxisWriter. It preserves provenance and keeps gaps visible before export.
entries.limits: It drafts the work product; the analyst still owns source review, tone, and final judgment.
